svg.aria-label: Committee discussion workflow: private opening rankings, support-based shortlist, two discussion rounds with a chair synthesis, a proposal slate, private final ballots, instant-runoff voting, and a saved decision record.
svg.text: How the simulated Nobel Committee decides
Eight agents, each conditioned on a real 2026 committee member, take a blinded longlist to a single prize decision.
No one sees anyone else's ranking
Ranked ballots, counted to a majority
Each member gets only their own profile and the
shuffled, blinded longlist, then ranks 8 candidates
and proposes up to three laureates for each.
A candidate advances with at least one first place,
two top-three rankings, or three top-eight rankings.
Nomination counts never enter the committee room.
the chair (gold pin) writes a neutral summary between rounds
Members read every opening ballot, answer at least
two colleagues and back one prize configuration.
The chair summarises support and open questions.
Each member must address what is still unresolved:
the science, who deserves credit, and whether the
discovery is mature enough for a prize.
proposal. P000, no award, is always on the slate.
Every member ranks every proposal exactly once.
Five votes win. Otherwise the weakest proposal is
eliminated and its ballots move to the next choice.
Each step is saved as a versioned JSON record,
so any simulated decision can be replayed.
